concepts.name: Node as server-side runtime
concepts.summary: Recall that Node.js runs JavaScript on the V8 engine outside the browser and exposes system APIs such as files and networking instead of the DOM.

concepts.name: Running scripts from terminal
concepts.summary: Run a file with the node command and use the REPL to try out expressions.

concepts.name: CommonJS require and exports
concepts.summary: Explain how require loads another file or built-in module and how module.exports determines what a file shares.

concepts.name: package.json and dependencies
concepts.summary: Understand that package.json describes a project and its dependencies, and that npm install fetches them into node_modules.

concepts.name: npm scripts
concepts.summary: Explain that the scripts field names shell commands that can be run with npm run, such as start and test.

concepts.name: Built-in core modules
concepts.summary: Name core modules such as fs, path, http and os that ship with Node and need no installation.

concepts.name: The process object basics
concepts.summary: Understand that process gives access to command-line arguments, environment variables and the current working directory.

misconceptions.text: Node.js is a programming language rather than a runtime for JavaScript.
Browser globals like window and document are available in Node.
Core modules like fs must be installed with npm before use.

concepts.name: Reading and writing files with fs
concepts.summary: Read, write and append files using callback, promise and sync variants of fs and choose the non-blocking form in servers.

concepts.name: Portable paths with path
concepts.summary: Build file paths with path.join and path.resolve and __dirname rather than concatenating strings.

concepts.name: ES modules in Node
concepts.summary: Write import and export syntax and enable ES modules through the .mjs extension or the type field, noting differences from CommonJS.

concepts.name: Semantic versioning and lockfiles
concepts.summary: Interpret version ranges such as ^ and ~ and explain why a lockfile pins exact installed versions.

concepts.name: Dev versus runtime dependencies
concepts.summary: Place packages in dependencies or devDependencies according to whether production code needs them.

concepts.name: Basic HTTP server
concepts.summary: Create a server with http.createServer that reads the request method and URL and writes a status, headers and body.

concepts.name: Buffers and binary data
concepts.summary: Create Buffers from strings and convert them back with an encoding such as utf8 or base64.

concepts.name: Event loop ordering basics
concepts.summary: Predict the order of synchronous code, timers, promises and I/O callbacks at a basic level.

misconceptions.text: Relative paths in fs calls resolve from the script's folder rather than the current working directory.
Using readFileSync is fine in a request handler because it is simpler.
require and import can be mixed freely in any file with no restrictions.

concepts.name: Express routing
concepts.summary: Define routes by method and path, read params, query and body, and organise them with Router.

concepts.name: Middleware chain and next
concepts.summary: Analyse how middleware runs in registration order and how calling next, responding or throwing controls the flow.

concepts.name: Express error handling
concepts.summary: Centralise errors with four-argument middleware and forward async failures to it correctly.

concepts.name: REST API design
concepts.summary: Model resources with nouns, correct methods and meaningful status codes, and validate input before use.

concepts.name: EventEmitter pattern
concepts.summary: Register listeners with on and once, emit events with arguments, and handle the special error event.

concepts.name: Streams and piping
concepts.summary: Process large data in chunks with readable and writable streams and connect them with pipe or pipeline.

concepts.name: Environment configuration
concepts.summary: Keep ports, credentials and settings in environment variables rather than in source code.

concepts.name: Building CLI tools
concepts.summary: Build a command-line tool that parses arguments, sets exit codes and is exposed through the bin field with a shebang.

misconceptions.text: Middleware order does not matter in Express.
Throwing inside an async route handler is always caught by Express error middleware.
Reading a whole file into memory is equivalent to streaming it for large files.

concepts.name: Event loop phases
concepts.summary: Analyse how libuv phases, the microtask queue and process.nextTick determine callback ordering and starvation.

concepts.name: Backpressure in streams
concepts.summary: Diagnose memory growth caused by ignoring write return values and apply drain handling or pipeline to fix it.

concepts.name: Worker threads and clustering
concepts.summary: Choose between worker threads, cluster and child processes for CPU-bound work or multi-core scaling.

concepts.name: Authentication and security middleware
concepts.summary: Evaluate session and token authentication, input validation and header and rate-limit protections for an API.

concepts.name: Testing Node services
concepts.summary: Design unit and HTTP integration tests that isolate I/O with mocks or test servers.

concepts.name: Profiling and memory leaks
concepts.summary: Use the inspector, CPU profiles and heap snapshots to locate blocking code and leaks.

concepts.name: Graceful shutdown and process signals
concepts.summary: Judge how to handle signals, close servers and drain connections, and why to restart after uncaught exceptions.

concepts.name: Module resolution and interop
concepts.summary: Analyse how Node resolves modules and how the exports map, dynamic import and CJS-ESM interop affect packages.

misconceptions.text: Node.js is single-threaded in every respect, so it cannot use multiple cores or threads.
Async functions make CPU-heavy work non-blocking.
Catching uncaughtException and carrying on keeps the process safe.

concepts.name: Scalable service architecture
concepts.summary: Design stateless Node services with queues, caching and load balancing that scale and fail gracefully.

concepts.name: Performance tradeoff evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate frameworks, serialization and concurrency choices using reproducible benchmarks and latency percentiles.

concepts.name: Native addons and N-API
concepts.summary: Judge when native addons or WebAssembly justify their build and portability costs.

concepts.name: Custom stream implementations
concepts.summary: Create Transform and custom streams that respect backpressure and error propagation for data pipelines.

concepts.name: Observability design
concepts.summary: Build logging, metrics and distributed tracing, including AsyncLocalStorage context, into services.

concepts.name: Package publishing and supply chain
concepts.summary: Design and publish reusable packages with sound versioning, exports and dependency vetting.

concepts.name: V8 and runtime internals
concepts.summary: Evaluate how V8 compilation, hidden classes and garbage collection affect code performance and memory.

misconceptions.text: Rewriting hot paths in native code always yields net speedups.
Adding more Node processes always improves throughput linearly.
Micro-benchmarks of isolated functions reliably predict production performance.
